root_cause: run_posix_cpu_timers() could still handle timers for a non-autoreaping task that had already passed exit_notify(), after which the task could be reaped while a concurrent posix_cpu_timer_del() could not see that the timer was firing; commit 0bdd2ed4 had removed the ->exit_state check, and the fix restores an exit_state early return.
notes: Fixes: 0bdd2ed4138e ('sched: run_posix_cpu_timers: Don't check ->exit_state, use lock_task_sighand()'). Mainline fix in 6.16; the CVE record lists stable fixes for 5.4 through 6.15. The patch was read from the GitHub mirror because git.kernel.org blocks automated fetching.

root_cause: The Extigy and Mbox 2/3 boot quirks re-read the USB device descriptor into dev->descriptor, overwriting bNumConfigurations without checking that it did not exceed the count usb_get_configuration() had used to allocate dev->config, so later code walked past the array; the fix reads into a temporary descriptor and validates bNumConfigurations before updating the device descriptor.
notes: Fixes: 1da177e4c3f4 (present since the initial git import). Mainline fix in 6.13. Needs a malicious USB device that the Extigy or Mbox quirks match.

root_cause: The validators used while walking USB-audio clock source, clock selector and clock multiplier descriptors did not check each descriptor's bLength (nor, for UAC2 and UAC3 selectors, the bNrInPins array and the fields after it), so a short descriptor from the device caused out-of-bounds reads; the fix adds length checks and skips descriptors that are too short.
notes: The mainline commit has no Fixes: tag; the CVE record gives b8e4f1fdfa422398c2d6c47bfb7d1feb3046d70a as the introducing commit. Mainline fix in 6.13. holdout-1.md relied on the CVE record only; the patch was read here from the GitHub mirror. Needs a malicious USB device.

root_cause: hid_alloc_report_buf() allocated the report buffer with kmalloc() instead of kzalloc(), so when a device sent a short report the unwritten part of the buffer carried old kernel memory onward; the fix zero-initializes the buffer.
notes: Fixes: 27ce405039bf ('HID: fix data access in implement()'). Mainline fix in 6.12. Needs a malicious HID device.

root_cause: After commit 72548b093ee3 switched algif_aead to in-place operation, the tag pages, which may be page-cache pages supplied from user space, were chained into the writable destination scatterlist, so the AEAD operation could write into them; the fix reverts algif_aead to out-of-place operation and only copies the associated data.
notes: Fixes: 72548b093ee3 ('crypto: algif_aead - copy AAD from src to dst'); affected from 4.14 per the CVE record. Mainline fix in 7.0. The fix commit message only says source and destination come from different mappings; the detail that page-cache pages get written comes from the xint analysis and was rated medium confidence in holdout-1.md. The lore announcement could not be read. audit_scope lists the three AF_ALG files because the fix changes shared helpers in af_alg.c and their callers.

classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: In __ip6_append_data(), the paged allocation branch computed alloclen without fraggap and pagedlen with it, so the linear area was fraggap bytes too small while the paged length was overstated, and the copy wrote past skb->end into skb_shared_info; the fix adds fraggap to alloclen and subtracts it from pagedlen, matching the non-paged branch.
notes: holdout-1.md cites 14200d435af9, which is a stable backport: its message says 'Upstream commit: 736b380e28d0'. The mainline fix 736b380e is used for the refs. Fixes: 773ba4fe9104 ('ipv6: avoid partial copy for zc'); affected 6.0 to 7.1.2 per the CVE record. Per the CVE description it is reached on UDPv6 with MSG_MORE and MSG_SPLICE_PAGES.

classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: unix_stream_recv_urg() left consumed zero-length out-of-band skbs on the receive queue, so several could sit in a row, which the SO_PEEK_OFF read path, ioctl(SIOCATMARK) and manage_oob() did not handle, leading to use after free; the fix removes the previously consumed OOB skb so consumed OOB skbs no longer pile up.
notes: Fixes: 314001f0bf92 ('af_unix: Add OOB support'); affected from 5.15. Mainline fix in 6.16. Reported by Jann Horn. Reachable by an unprivileged local user through AF_UNIX stream sockets with MSG_OOB.

root_cause: hfsc_enqueue() judged whether a class was already in the eligible tree by cl->cl_nactive, which only the init_vf path maintains; a class that goes through init_ed instead (a real-time-only class), combined with a reentrant enqueue from a child qdisc such as netem, was inserted into the eltree twice; the fix checks tree membership directly with a new cl_in_el_or_vttree() helper.
notes: Fixes: 37d9cf1a3ce3 ('sched: Fix detection of empty queues in child qdiscs'). Mainline fix in 6.16. The double insertion shows up as use after free or an endless loop when combined with netem as a child qdisc, per the commit message.

root_cause: io_futex_wait() assigned the preallocated io_futex_data to req->async_data without setting REQ_F_ASYNC_DATA, and its failure path freed the data without clearing req->async_data; the fix sets the flag together with the pointer and clears both on the failure path.
notes: Fixes: 194bb58c6090 ('io_uring: add support for futex wake and wait'); affected from 6.7. Mainline fix in 6.17. What REQ_F_ASYNC_DATA means (who frees async_data) is defined in io_uring core outside futex.c, so the auditor may need to read that too.

root_cause: __bpf_ringbuf_reserve() decided whether a new record would overlap older ones using the consumer position, which user space can write, so a new reservation could overlap a record that was reserved but not yet committed and overwrite its header; the fix tracks the oldest pending record position (pending_pos) in the kernel and rejects reservations whose span from it exceeds the ring size.
notes: Fixes: 457f44363a88 ('bpf: Implement BPF ring buffer and verifier support'). Mainline fix in 6.10. holdout-1.md relied on the CVE record only; the patch was read here from the GitHub mirror.

root_cause: move_normal_pmd() read the PMD and decided to move a whole page table while holding only mmap_lock, and took the rmap locks afterwards, so retract_page_tables() in khugepaged, which runs without mmap or VMA lock, could remove the page table in between; the fix rechecks under the locks that the PMD is still present and not a leaf before moving it.
notes: Fixes: 1d65b771bc08 ('mm/khugepaged: retract_page_tables() without mmap or vma lock'); affected 6.6 to 6.11.4. Mainline fix in 6.12. Only mm/mremap.c is patched; the racing side retract_page_tables() is in mm/khugepaged.c. Per the CVE description it needs concurrent mremap() and MADV_COLLAPSE on a shared tmpfs mapping.

root_cause: The execute permission check happened when the file was opened, but bprm_fill_uid() read the owner and mode much later to decide on setuid/setgid, and the metadata could change in between; the fix re-checks execute permission with inode_permission() under the inode lock where the ids are read, and does not apply set-id if the check fails.
notes: The mainline commit has no Fixes: tag; the CVE record gives 9167b0b9a0ab7907191523f5a0528e3b9c288e21 as the introducing commit. Mainline fix in 6.11.

root_cause: Commit 6d98eb95b450 replaced the binder_alloc_copy_from_buffer() calls in binder_get_object() with copy_from_user(), which dropped the offset alignment check that check_buffer() had done implicitly; the fix adds an explicit !IS_ALIGNED(offset, sizeof(u32)) check.
notes: Fixes: 6d98eb95b450 ('binder: avoid potential data leakage when copying txn'). The commit message adds that the check existed before 7a67a39320df and was likely removed then as redundant. Mainline fix in 6.9. holdout-1.md relied on the CVE record only; the patch was read here from the GitHub mirror. The lost check was done implicitly by check_buffer() behind binder_alloc_copy_from_buffer(), so hand the auditor the whole drivers/android directory rather than binder.c alone.

classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: clone_private_mount() only refused a source mount with MNT_LOCKED children and did not check that the caller has CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the user namespace that owns the source mount's namespace; the fix adds ns_capable(old_mnt->mnt_ns->user_ns, CAP_SYS_ADMIN).
notes: Fixes: 427215d85e8d ('ovl: prevent private clone if bind mount is not allowed'); the CVE record lists several introducing commits across stable branches. Mainline fix in 6.16. The commit message notes that other CAP_SYS_ADMIN checks during mounting usually, but not always, covered the missing one.

root_cause: smb2_session_logoff() freed sess->user while another connection binding to the same session could still be using it in smb2_sess_setup(); the fix removes the free and the NULL assignment from the logoff path.
notes: The mainline commit has no Fixes: tag; the CVE record gives 0626e6641f6b467447c81dd7678a69c66f7746cf as the introducing commit. Mainline fix in 6.15. Needs a second connection that binds to the same session while the first one logs off.

root_cause: When ngx_http_parse_complex_uri() handled '/../' it moved the output pointer back and walked back to the previous '/', but checked the lower bound of the URI buffer only once before the loop and not at each step, so the walk could go below the start of the buffer; the fix checks the bound on every step of the backward walk.
notes: Git commit 97aa4c8 ('handle "/../" case more reliably', 2009-09-14) has the same change as the published patch. Vulnerable 0.1.0-0.8.14; fixed in 0.8.15, 0.7.62, 0.6.39 and 0.5.38.

root_cause: The proxy, fastcgi, scgi and uwsgi modules allocated each upstream response header from the parsed key and value lengths but filled it with ngx_cpystrn(), which stops at a NUL byte, and the header parser accepted NUL bytes, so the unwritten rest of the buffer, holding old freed memory, was sent to the client at the original length; the fix copies with ngx_memcpy() plus explicit termination and rejects header lines containing NUL.
notes: Fix spans two commits: eb526b7 ('Fixed incorrect ngx_cpystrn() usage in ngx_http_*_process_header()') and its child d1ed97b ('Headers with null character are now rejected'); the published patch combines both. Vulnerable 0.1.0-1.1.16; fixed in 1.1.17 and 1.0.14. NVD classifies it as use after free, but the patch shows a truncated copy into an uninitialized buffer. The same pattern is in the fastcgi, scgi and uwsgi modules, so any one of them works as the audit target.

root_cause: ngx_http_parse_chunked() accumulated the hexadecimal chunk size into a signed integer with no overflow or sign check, so a large size could become negative and be passed on as a length; the fix rejects a negative ctx->size or ctx->length.
notes: Git commit 818807d ('Fixed chunk size parsing.') has the same change as the published patch. Vulnerable 1.3.9-1.4.0; fixed in 1.5.0 and 1.4.1. The advisory describes the result as a stack-based buffer overflow; the memory corruption happens where the negative size is consumed, outside the parser, but the root cause is the missing check in the parser.

root_cause: In ngx_http_parse_request_line(), on an unescaped space inside the URI the parser switched to the sw_check_uri or sw_uri state after the current character had already been consumed, and the new state did not examine it again, so that character skipped the URI checks; the fix steps back one character (p--) so the new state re-reads it.
notes: Git commit d47c435 ('Proper backtracking after space in a request line.') has the same change as the published patch. Vulnerable 0.8.41-1.5.6; fixed in 1.5.7 and 1.4.4.

root_cause: ngx_http_spdy_state_save() copied the rest of an incomplete frame into the fixed-size state buffer, but the check that the data fits NGX_SPDY_STATE_BUFFER_SIZE was compiled only under NGX_DEBUG, so release builds had no bound; the fix makes the check unconditional.
notes: Git commit c6c702c ('SPDY: always check size of data to be saved into state buffer.') has the same change as the published patch; later commits 062e7a0 and ec1211d refine the same check. Vulnerable 1.3.15-1.5.11 with the SPDY module; fixed in 1.5.12 and 1.4.7. Audit a release (non-debug) build configuration.

classes: Assumptions broken by callbacks and reentrancy
root_cause: ngx_mail_smtp_starttls() did not discard the read buffer when switching to TLS, so SMTP commands pipelined in plaintext behind STARTTLS stayed buffered and were processed as if they had arrived inside the encrypted session; the fix resets s->buffer pos and last to the start of the buffer.
notes: Git commit 44f45a5 ('Mail: discard pipelined commands after SMTP STARTTLS.') has the same change as the published patch; its message says the bug appeared in 1.5.6. Vulnerable 1.5.6-1.7.3; fixed in 1.7.4 and 1.6.1. Only the SMTP handler is patched.

root_cause: When a request body chain was written to a temporary file, ngx_chain_to_iovec() (ngx_write_chain_to_file() before 1.9.13) did not skip special buffers that carry no data and used their pointers in length arithmetic, which led to a NULL pointer dereference; the fix skips buffers for which ngx_buf_special() is true.
notes: Git commit a3d3823 ('Core: skip special buffers on writing (ticket #981)') is the mainline fix and matches patch.2016.write.txt (for 1.9.13-1.11.0, ngx_chain_to_iovec); patch.2016.write2.txt is the same fix for 1.3.9-1.9.12 in ngx_write_chain_to_file. Vulnerable 1.3.9-1.11.0; fixed in 1.11.1 and 1.10.1. Special buffers reach this code through chunked request bodies.

root_cause: The HTTP/2 module processed PRIORITY frames without any count limit, so a peer could keep reshuffling stream priorities and make the server spend CPU on priority tree updates; the fix adds a per-connection priority_limit, set from concurrent_streams, decremented on each PRIORITY frame and refilled when a stream is created, and closes the connection with ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM when it runs out.
notes: The advisory has no patch link; 39bb3b9 ('HTTP/2: limited number of PRIORITY frames.', 2019-08-13) is the fix commit in the official repository. Vulnerable 1.9.5-1.17.2; fixed in 1.17.3 and 1.16.1.

root_cause: ap_invoke_handler() used r->content_type as the handler name when no handler was set, without telling whether the content type came from server configuration or from a backend response header, so a backend response could select a local handler; the fix adds ap_set_content_type_ex() with a trusted flag (AP_REQUEST_TRUSTED_CT) and uses the content type as a handler only when it is trusted.
notes: Commit 554554b is on the 2.4.x branch ('Merge r1918551 from trunk'); the httpd advisory cites svn r1918560 for 2.4.x. Affected 2.4.0-2.4.59; fixed in 2.4.60. The fix touches 11 files because every module that sets a content type from configuration now marks it trusted; the key decision is the one-line change in ap_invoke_handler. After the fix some AddType-to-handler configurations must move to SetHandler.

classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: In server context, mod_rewrite decided whether a substitution result is a file-system path or a URL path by checking with prefix_stat() whether its first segment exists on disk, even when that segment came from a backreference or variable, so a request could map a URL onto a file-system location no URL was meant to reach; the fix requires the new UnsafePrefixStat flag for such substitutions.
notes: Commit 9a6157d is on trunk (git-svn-id trunk@1918552), so the refs are trunk refs. The 2.4.x merge is svn r1918561 per the httpd advisory; its git hash was not found in the mirror. For a release-based test use the 2.4.59 release (affected) and 2.4.60 (fixed). The same commit also adds the UnsafeAllow3F flag for encoded question marks, which is not part of this root cause.

root_cause: sample_conv_regsub() computed the room left for each back-reference replacement from the output buffer (output->size - output->data) while the replacements were written into the temporary trash buffer, so replacing many short matches with a longer string could overflow the trash buffer; the fix computes the room from the trash buffer.
notes: The fix message says the bug came with commit 07e1e3c (2.2; hash abbreviated there) and asks for backport to all supported versions. Affected 2.2 through 3.1.6 per the CVE record. Only configurations that use regsub with global replacement of several matches are affected. The GitHub repository mirrors git.haproxy.org.

root_cause: h2_release_mbuf() emptied the HTTP/2 mux output buffers without clearing the H2_CF_MUX_MFULL and H2_CF_DEM_MROOM flags, so after a GOAWAY was sent and the buffers were released the flags still said 'full' and h2_send() looped forever; the fix clears both flags whenever the buffers are released.
notes: Fixed in 3.0.4 and 2.9.10. Per the commit message the state is reached mainly with zero-copy forwarding (3.0) and the glitches limit, though it could in theory happen earlier; the message also asks to backport a related consistency-check commit, which was not identified. Mitigation per the HAProxy blog: tune.h2.zero-copy-fwd-send off.

root_cause: When internal_address_config was empty, DefaultInternalAddressConfig::isInternalAddress() still treated every RFC1918 private address as internal, so requests from any client on a private network were marked internal and kept their x-envoy headers instead of having them cleaned; the fix adds the runtime guard envoy.reloadable_features.explicit_internal_address_config, under which an empty configuration treats no address as internal.
notes: The advisory has no commit link. 0ee424bb ('internal_address_config: change the default to be more secure for service mesh environments') comes from PR #36221 ('[IMPORTANT] Multiple CVEs') and adds exactly the runtime guard the advisory names. In the fixed releases (1.31.2, 1.30.6, 1.29.9, 1.28.7) the guard defaults to false, so the old default stays until an operator enables it or fills internal_address_config; commit ca73fe4 (2025-07-24, title only read) later removed the flag and the legacy code path. At the vulnerable ref, mutateRequestHeaders() in conn_manager_utility.cc calls isInternalAddress() and cleans internal headers only for non-internal requests.

root_cause: The proxy_protocol listener filter copied raw TLV bytes into a protobuf string value in dynamic metadata without UTF-8 validation, so the ext_authz check request built from that metadata failed, and with failure_mode_allow set that failure was treated as allowed; the fix replaces non-UTF-8 bytes with MessageUtil::sanitizeUtf8String() before storing TLV values.
notes: Fix commit is on main (PR #32300, 'Assorted CVE fixes'); fixed in 1.29.1, 1.28.1, 1.27.3 and 1.26.7. Needs PROXY protocol with TLVs copied into metadata and ext_authz with failure_mode_allow: true. The fix is only on the producer side; the fail-open behavior of ext_authz is configuration, so an audit of the ext_authz filter alone will not find the missing validation.

root_cause: In tls_post_process_server_rpk() the client used the result of ssl_verify_rpk() only to decide whether to retry (SSL_RETRY_VERIFY), and on a verification failure it did not abort the handshake even when SSL_VERIFY_PEER was set; the fix sends a fatal alert when verification fails under SSL_VERIFY_PEER.
notes: Fix commit is on the openssl-3.4 branch (3.4.1); 3.3.3 and 3.2.4 are also fixed. Affected 3.2 to 3.4. Only clients that enable server raw public keys (RFC 7250, off by default) and rely on the handshake failing are affected; calling SSL_get_verify_result() still shows the failure.

root_cause: do_x509_check() let otherName subject alternative names through its type filter (for SmtpUTF8Mailbox email checks) and later read the GENERAL_NAME union member that matches the check type rather than the entry's actual type, so an otherName of another kind was read through the wrong member; the fix switches on gen->type and the otherName type_id and ignores unexpected encodings.
notes: The fix commit was found on the openssl-3.2 branch (3.2.3); 3.3.2, 3.1.7 and 3.0.15 are also fixed. Affected 3.0 to 3.3. Reached when an application checks an expected name against a certificate that has an otherName SAN (for example TLS clients checking server certificates).
